saml.description: If the SAML identity provider configuration leaves Identity Provider Entity ID empty, Keycloak does not validate the Issuer of received SAML assertions.
saml.note: Issuer-mismatch acceptance is by design when this field is unset.

saml.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled.
saml.note: Case-only identity differences may collapse by design.

saml.description: During first broker login, Keycloak may link to an existing local account with the same email or username depending on the configured first login flow.
saml.note: Account linking during first login is configurable behavior, not necessarily an identity-binding flaw.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, brokered email addresses are trusted and may be marked verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode.
saml.note: Email-based linking or verified-email state changes can be configuration-driven.

saml.description: Automatically Set Existing User / AutoLink style first-login flows can link existing accounts without verification.
saml.note: This is explicitly documented as dangerous; treat as admin-configured behavior, not a product bug by itself.

saml.description: Additional MFA after identity-provider login only occurs when a Post Login Flow is configured.
saml.note: Absence of MFA after broker login is expected unless post-login flow enforces it.

saml.description: If an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization group mappings are preserved but no longer active; authentication still succeeds.
saml.note: Missing organization-group assignment after unlink is by design and should not be flagged as authorization inconsistency.

saml.constraint: For SAML issuer-validation tests (I1 saml_issuer_mismatch), create_provider MUST set identity_provider_entity_id (config.idpEntityId). If this field is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation for received SAML assertions.

For SAML signature-validation tests (I1 saml_cert_substitution), create_provider MUST explicitly set validate_signature=true and want_assertions_signed=true when testing secure configurations. If validate_signature is OFF, Keycloak does not expect signed SAML requests/responses from the external IdP.

To test insecure defaults for SAML signature handling, create_provider with default SAML config and then saml_login is meaningful because documentation states Validate Signature and Want Assertions Signed are configurable expectations rather than always-on checks.

Principal binding semantics: principal_type selects either Subject NameID or a SAML attribute, and principal_attribute names the exact attribute/friendly-name to use. There is no documented wildcard or regex companion for these fields. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT set principal_attribute to '*' expecting wildcard behavior; omit restrictive principal selection or use a stable exact attribute.

Case handling: if case_sensitive_username is disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating users. For I4 case_confusion tests, explicitly control this setting because 'Admin' and 'admin' may collapse by design when case-sensitive username is OFF.

For I4 account-linking and collision tests, First Login Flow materially changes behavior. The default first broker login flow may create a new user if unique, or prompt/link existing accounts by email/reauthentication. A valid collision test must pin the first_login_flow_alias and not interpret first-login linking behavior as spontaneous identity collapse.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, trust_email MUST be considered. When Trust Email is ON, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on federation depending on sync mode. Do not treat email-based linking/verification outcomes as bugs unless trust_email and first-login flow are configured to disallow that trust path.

For I4 repeated-login profile update tests, sync_mode affects whether brokered attributes are updated on subsequent logins. 'import' does not update user data, while 'force' updates when possible. Do not interpret unchanged or changed profile fields across logins as identity confusion without controlling sync_mode.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, additional authentication after broker login is BY DESIGN only when a Post Login Flow is configured. If post_login_flow_alias is unset, successful SAML login without MFA does not prove bypass. Configure a post-login flow that enforces OTP/MFA before testing.

For I3 config-change sequences, changes to identity provider configuration or authentication flows affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same login pattern before and after config change, not treat an admin reconfiguration itself as a bug.

SAML flow is session-bound to an SP-initiated request. saml_login MUST initiate the broker login flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo correlation; posting a fabricated SAMLResponse without initiating the flow will be rejected for protocol reasons rather than security enforcement.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, usually 30 minutes by default. Multi-step browser/SAML sequences must complete within the authentication session lifetime or restart the flow; otherwise failures are due to expired authentication session, not assertion validation.

Numeric sentinel: password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses value 0 as a literal strict sentinel meaning the user must always re-authenticate before password update; it does not mean default or disabled.

Numeric sentinel: password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses value -1 to mean use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing iterations. Defaults depend on algorithm (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000).

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn timeout value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; documentation says behavior depends on authenticator implementation. Never assume timeout=0 disables or strictly enforces timeout.
Numeric sentinel: user session count limiter uses 0 as disabled for both maximum realm sessions and maximum client sessions. Do not interpret 0 as zero allowed sessions.

Numeric sentinel: authenticationSessions SPI authSessionsLimit default is 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session; when limit is reached, oldest sub-session is removed. Tests opening many parallel auth tabs may evict older sub-sessions by design.

For SAML client audience/recipient tests, the SAML client Client ID must match the issuer value sent with AuthnRequests. Keycloak matches the client by issuer from the AuthnRequest. Misconfigured client_id/issuer causes routing failure unrelated to audience enforcement.
For SAML client redirect URI tests, Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. Do not use mid-string wildcards when testing redirect validation.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set validateSignature=true and wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states that if Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, no Issuer validation is performed, and signature validation is controlled by Validate Signature / Want Assertions Signed switches. Default-config acceptance without these fields is not evidence of a bug unless the test intentionally targets insecure defaults.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution insecure-default testing, the fuzzer MUST create the SAML IdP with default/minimal config and intentionally omit validateSignature and wantAssertionsSigned. If forged SAML login succeeds in that setup, treat it as insecure default behavior under test; if the fuzzer sets either flag, the test no longer measures the documented default.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure create_provider/enable_auth_method with identity_provider_entity_id (config.idpEntityId). The documentation explicitly says: if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Without this field, issuer-mismatch tests are invalid and may produce false positives or trivial acceptance.

For I1/I5 audience tests on SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST create a SAML client/application and use its actual SP entity ID as the expected audience. The docs state the client ID is the expected issuer in SAML requests and the broker SP entity ID defaults to the realm base URL unless overridden. Wrong assumptions about SP entity ID will invalidate saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertion replay and OneTimeUse replay MUST use the same Assertion ID across two saml_login events. The attack sequence should use fixed_assertion_id consistently. A second login with a different assertion ID is not a replay test.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a control saml_login without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Otherwise a failed expired assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken provider/client setup or first-login-flow issues.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving brokered SAML login, remember that authentication sessions expire after the Login timeout (30 minutes by default). The same browser flow is session-bound; if the auth session expires between SP initiation and SAMLResponse submission, rejection is by design and not an invariant violation.

For I3 config-change tests, changing identity provider settings or client settings affects NEW logins by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent fresh logins before and after the change, not expect an already-started browser/authentication session to survive arbitrary admin reconfiguration.

For I4 principal-binding tests, SAML Principal Type controls which assertion field identifies the external user: Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. The fuzzer MUST keep this setting fixed and known during a test. Changing Principal Type changes the identity key by design and can make two different upstream identities collapse or diverge for non-security reasons.

For I4 tests using transient NameID, do NOT configure principal_type=SUBJECT with nameid_policy_format=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient. The documentation states Subject NameID value cannot be set together with transient NameID Policy Format. Such a setup is invalid and any failure is not security-relevant.

For I4 case-sensitivity tests, the fuzzer MUST account for the identity provider setting Case-sensitive username. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating, while server usernames are always lower-case. 'Admin' and 'admin' collapsing is by design in that mode, not necessarily a bug.

For I4 email-linking and account-takeover tests, First Login Flow selection is security-critical. The default first broker login flow does NOT automatically link existing accounts without checks; automatic linking only occurs if administrators configure dangerous flows such as Automatically Set Existing User / AutoLink. The fuzzer must record which first login flow is configured before treating account linking as a vulnerability.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, Trust Email MUST be considered. If trust_email is enabled, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode. Auto-linking or verification outcomes under trust_email=true are by configuration and must not be conflated with bypasses under trust_email=false.

For I4 organization/group mapping tests, Advanced Claim to Group mapper claim values support two modes: exact match by default, or regex when Regex Claim Values is enabled. For multi-identity scenarios, exact-match claim constraints MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-like values. Regex semantics exist only when the explicit regex toggle is enabled.

For I5 authorization-binding tests on roles in tokens/assertions, Keycloak limits effective roles to the intersection of user-assigned roles and client role scope mappings. Tests for over-granting must configure both user roles and client scope mappings deliberately; otherwise missing roles in the token/assertion are by design, not under-grant bugs.

For I5 scope/downscoping tests, client scopes with role scope mappings apply only if the user is permitted to use them. If a user lacks intersection with the scope's roles, protocol mappers and role mappings from that client scope are omitted. Do not treat missing claims or groups as inconsistent authorization unless user-permission to the scope was established.

For I5 SAML OneTimeUse generation tests from Keycloak as IdP/SP, Include OneTimeUse Condition on a SAML client controls whether Keycloak includes OneTimeUse in login responses it issues. This is unrelated to whether the broker enforces OneTimeUse on inbound assertions from an external IdP. Do not confuse outbound assertion generation settings with inbound validation behavior.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy Hashing iterations uses -1 as a sentinel meaning use the algorithm default iteration count; it does NOT mean disable hashing or zero iterations. Defaults documented are algorithm-specific (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.

Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 to mean always require re-authentication before password update. Value 0 is literal strict behavior, not 'use default' and not 'disable'. Tests that rely on password-update reauth must treat 0 as strongest enforcement.

Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 to disable the session-limit check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Value 0 is a disable sentinel, not literal zero allowed sessions. Do not interpret login success under 0 as a bypass.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn timeout uses 0 to defer behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation. Value 0 is not a guaranteed immediate timeout and not a fixed zero-second limit. Timing tests must not assume deterministic expiry when timeout=0.

Numeric sentinel: Client secret rotation uses Rotated Secret Expiration=0 to remove the old secret immediately during rotation. Value 0 is a special immediate-expiry sentinel, not 'keep forever' and not 'use default'. Secret Expiration and Rotated Secret Expiration are evaluated at policy execution time.

Session-use budget: the documentation includes token revocation and userinfo/introspection endpoints, but no per-token num_uses limit for OIDC access tokens is documented in the provided material. Therefore the fuzzer should not infer a reusable-call budget from unrelated session-limit or auth-session-limit settings; those limit concurrent sessions/subsessions, not bearer-token API call count.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution tests, create the SAML IdP with DEFAULT config and do NOT set validateSignature=true or wantAssertionsSigned=true if you are testing insecure defaults. The documentation states Validate Signature controls whether requests and responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether signed Assertions are expected. If these are left unset/off, acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned assertions may be by configuration rather than a validation bypass.

Identity Provider Entity ID performs Issuer validation for received SAML assertions. If this field is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST set identity_provider_entity_id on the brokered SAML provider for enforcement tests. For insecure-default tests, omit it intentionally and interpret acceptance as issuer validation being skipped by configuration.

Validate Signature and Want Assertions Signed are distinct controls. Validate Signature covers whether SAML requests/responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed; Want Assertions Signed indicates whether the SP expects a signed Assertion specifically. For saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests, the fuzzer MUST enable Want Assertions Signed when testing assertion-level integrity. Otherwise acceptance of a response-signed but assertion-unsigned message may be by configuration, not an I1 violation.

Use metadata descriptor URL changes trust-anchor behavior. When ON, validating certificates are automatically downloaded and cached from Metadata descriptor URL; when OFF, certificates in Validating X509 Certificates are used. For I1 trust-anchor and key-substitution tests, the fuzzer MUST control this setting explicitly and avoid stale-cache confusion. If testing static trust, set use_metadata_descriptor_url=false and provide validating_x509_certificates directly.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a CONTROL login with a fresh assertion before the replay attempt. A failed replay without a successful control cannot distinguish replay protection from broken provider setup, bad bindings, or first-login/account-linking flow issues.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, documented as 30 minutes by default. SAML broker flows are session-bound and SP-initiated. The fuzzer MUST complete the initiate_saml_flow and ACS submission within the same live authentication session; otherwise failures are due to expired auth session rather than SAML validation.

The authenticationSessions SPI parameter authSessionsLimit is a numeric sentinel-like limit on authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session. Default is 300; when the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed as new ones are created. Multi-tab or repeated SP-initiated SAML tests MUST avoid exhausting this budget, or flow restarts and mismatched InResponseTo errors may occur for reasons unrelated to I3.

For I3 flow-coherence tests, Keycloak documents that admin changes to identity provider configuration, authentication flows, or client settings legitimately affect NEW logins. A valid I3 test must show inconsistent handling of the SAME logical request/session, not merely that a later login used updated configuration.

First Login Flow can create, link, or re-authenticate users after brokered login. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST account for first-broker-login behavior because collisions or merges may be caused by configured account-linking flow rather than SAML principal parsing alone.

Automatically linking existing accounts is documented as dangerous. If the configured First Login Flow uses Automatically Set Existing User / AutoLink behavior, email- or username-based merges are by design and can cause apparent I4 violations. The fuzzer MUST record the configured first_login_flow and treat auto-linking flows as a known high-risk configuration, not an implementation bug by themselves.

Trust Email marks brokered email addresses as verified when enabled, and can update verification state on subsequent logins depending on sync mode. For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST set trust_email=false on the identity provider; otherwise email-based linking or verification changes may be by configuration.

Case-sensitive username affects only the username associated with the federated identity; usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, differences in brokered username case may collapse by design unless case_sensitive_username is enabled, and even then local usernames remain lower-cased. The fuzzer MUST not treat lowercasing of local usernames as a collision bug by itself.

Principal Type determines which SAML assertion component identifies the external user: Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. For I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST set principal_type explicitly and keep it constant across compared runs. Changing principal_type changes the identity key by design and invalidates collision conclusions.

Principal Attribute supports exact selection of an attribute name or friendly name; the documentation does not describe wildcard or regex matching for this field. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, the fuzzer MUST NOT set principal_attribute to '*' or pattern text expecting wildcard behavior. If multiple identities must pass, omit attribute-based principal selection or use a stable exact attribute name present in all assertions.

Essential claim value supports regular expression format, but this is a generic identity-provider filter on JWT tokens and not a SAML principal selector. If used on mixed broker configurations, regex-based filtering can broaden or narrow acceptance in ways that confound I4/I5 tests. The fuzzer MUST avoid enabling verify_essential_claim for SAML-focused tests unless the test explicitly targets that filter behavior.

Requested AuthnContext constraints are only enforced when ClassRefs or DeclRefs are present. If none are present, the Identity Provider does not enforce additional constraints. For SAML MFA/step-up related tests, the fuzzer MUST configure requested_authncontext_classrefs or requested_authncontext_declrefs explicitly; otherwise absence of MFA or stronger auth is by configuration.

Requested AuthnContext Comparison has semantic values Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better, defaulting to Exact. For step-up or MFA-related SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST set comparison deliberately because different comparison modes can satisfy requests with different authentication contexts and change outcomes without indicating a bypass.

For I5 audience-binding tests on SAML clients, assertions should include Conditions with AudienceRestriction matching the SP/client. The docs describe SAML assertions carrying Conditions and AudienceRestriction, and client settings rely on issuer/client matching. A missing Conditions or AudienceRestriction element may be accepted or rejected depending on client/SP configuration; include a valid control assertion first to distinguish setup failure from missing audience enforcement.

Valid Redirect URIs for SAML clients allow wildcards only at the end of a URL and are used when exact SAML endpoints are not registered and Keycloak pulls the Assertion Consumer URL from a request. For I5 authorization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST avoid permissive wildcard redirect patterns unless the test explicitly targets them, because broad ACS acceptance can mask audience/recipient binding issues.

Master SAML Processing URL is used for all SAML requests and responses unless request-specific ACS URLs take precedence, and it must match a registered Valid Redirect URI pattern. For SAML audience/recipient tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the client uses master URL or request ACS precedence; otherwise a response may be accepted at an unexpected endpoint by design.

Include OneTimeUse Condition on SAML clients is a client-side emission setting for Keycloak acting as IdP, not a broker-side enforcement toggle for incoming external assertions. The fuzzer MUST NOT infer that enabling or disabling this client setting changes broker replay protection for inbound SAML assertions.

Assertion Lifespan on SAML clients has sentinel semantics: if not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used instead of literal zero/empty. Never assume an unset value means no expiry. For timing-sensitive SAML tests, explicitly set assertion_lifespan when controlling downstream assertion validity.

Password policy Maximum Authentication Age has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before updating password, not disable the check. Never interpret 0 as unlimited. This matters when using password-based admin setup or re-authentication flows during broker linking tests.
Password policy Hashing iterations has sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing iterations. Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.

User session count limiter has sentinel semantics: value 0 disables the session-limit check for realm or client session counts. If enabled in browser, direct grant, reset credentials, or post broker login flows, it can deny or terminate sessions during SAML tests for reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
